thinkers.name: Aris Roussinos
thinkers.why: Originating UnHerd essay; still the cleanest short definition.
thinkers.guardrail: Journalist, not a mascot. Quote him, do not enlist him.

thinkers.name: Peter Diamandis
thinkers.one_line: Techno-optimist who argues exponential technologies can meet large human problems.
thinkers.why: An anchor for Anglofuturism's hyper-ambitions — abundance as an engineering claim, not a vibe.
thinkers.guardrail: American abundance talk. Steal the altitude, not the Californian costume.

thinkers.name: Dominic Cummings
thinkers.one_line: State capacity, elite performance, and high-throughput science.
thinkers.why: A policy engine: how a state that can still do things would actually be wired.
thinkers.guardrail: A former operator, not a saint. Read the method, not the memoir war.

thinkers.name: David Starkey
thinkers.one_line: Argues the English constitutional apparatus was an engine of global modernity.
thinkers.why: Historical grounding: law and parliament as technologies, not costume drama.
thinkers.guardrail: Historian with a polemic. Take the constitutional claim; leave the chat-show heat.

thinkers.name: Wyndham Lewis
thinkers.why: Founded the Vorticists — a modernist avant-garde rooted in an Anglo temperament, not Milanese theatre.
thinkers.guardrail: Esoteric categorisation only. BLAST is a magazine, not a political programme.

thinkers.name: Works in Progress
thinkers.one_line: The materialist, supply-side backbone of British techno-optimism.
thinkers.why: Suppliers of competence and know-how — housing, energy, and the unglamorous arithmetic of building.
thinkers.guardrail: A journal, not a ministry. Steal the numbers.

thinkers.name: Logos Movement
thinkers.one_line: Privacy-first builders of decentralised tools and local civic rooms.
thinkers.why: An embodiment of refusing the envelope — alternative futures that do not wait for a licence.
thinkers.guardrail: Exemplar, not a script. Parallel institutions, not a secession romance.

thinkers.name: John Ruskin
thinkers.one_line: Craft, hierarchy, and producer guilds against soulless mass-fabrication.
thinkers.why: A moral aesthetic: vernacular craft and human-scale dignity fused with the capacity to still make difficult things.
thinkers.guardrail: Borrow the aesthetics and the conviction only. Not a medieval LARP and not a soil-cult.

thinkers.name: The Wyvern Fellowship
thinkers.one_line: Preserving heritage, building resilience, securing a future.
thinkers.why: A national fellowship of people, families and local chapters for mutual support and cultural preservation across Britain.
thinkers.guardrail: Civic fellowship. Heritage as shared craft and mutual aid, not a soil-cult and not a party.

thinkers.name: Philip Cunliffe
thinkers.why: Political theory in the Anglofuturist key: what a country is for, once the official page has finished.
thinkers.guardrail: A theorist, not a foreign-policy mascot. Quote the argument.

thinkers.name: David Deutsch
thinkers.one_line: Quantum theory of computation and information.
thinkers.why: Hauling the future closer one qubit at a time — explanation as a British craft.
thinkers.guardrail: Physicist. Steal the method, not a costume.

thinkers.name: Matt Ridley
thinkers.one_line: The history of innovation, written as rational optimism.
thinkers.why: The degrowth antidote: prosperity as the product of ideas that are allowed to copy.
thinkers.guardrail: Rational optimist. Numbers and history, not a party officer.

thinkers.name: Free Speech Union
thinkers.one_line: For when you have already stepped outside the envelope.
thinkers.why: The practical defence of saying the unfiled thing out loud.
thinkers.guardrail: A union for speech. Not our membership desk and not a party mark.
